skill.name: iterate-pr
skill.description: Iterate on a pull request until CI checks pass and review feedback is handled using GitHub CLI workflows.
skill.summary: Guides an AI agent through PR checks, feedback review, fixes, commits, and CI waits.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The skill is not malicious, but it intentionally uses authenticated GitHub CLI and git commands. Most static backtick findings are Markdown formatting false positives, while the real risk is automated commit and push behavior plus CI log access.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before staging, committing, or pushing changes. Prefer staging only reviewed files instead of all files.
Resolve the branch name once, quote it in shell commands, and reject empty or unusual branch names before use.

remediation.issue: Authenticated GitHub CLI and API access
remediation.suggestion: Document required GitHub scopes and limit commands to the current repository and pull request.

remediation.issue: CI log inspection can expose sensitive details
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before fetching verbose logs and avoid copying secrets or tokens from CI output into responses.

static_findings.snippet: The `bucket` field categorizes state into: `pass`, `fail`, `pending`, `skipping`, or `cancel`.
**Important:** If any of these checks are still `pending`, wait before proceeding:
- All CI checks are green (`bucket: pass`)
- Use `gh pr checks --required` to focus only on required checks
- Use `gh run view <run-id> --verbose` to see all job steps, not just failures
4. **Skip invalid feedback** - If the concern is not legitimate, move on

content.value_statement: PR fixes often require repeated CI checks, review reading, commits, and pushes. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through that loop with GitHub CLI.
actual_capabilities: Identifies the pull request for the current branch.
Checks GitHub Actions and PR check status before editing.
Collects review comments, conversation comments, and bot feedback.
Inspects failed workflow logs before proposing fixes.
Guides targeted code changes, commits, pushes, and CI waiting.
limitations: Requires an authenticated GitHub CLI in the repository.
Can commit and push changes, so users should review diffs first.
Cannot resolve unclear reviewer decisions without user input.
Depends on GitHub and CI service availability.

use_cases.title: Fix failing PR checks
use_cases.description: Use the skill to inspect failed CI logs, make focused fixes, and wait for checks to complete.

use_cases.title: Address review feedback
use_cases.description: Use the skill to gather human and bot comments, verify each issue, and apply targeted updates.

use_cases.title: Prepare a merge-ready branch
use_cases.description: Use the skill to repeat checks and feedback review until the PR meets quality gates.

prompt_templates.title: Check my PR status
prompt_templates.prompt: Use iterate-pr to find the current pull request and summarize its CI status. Do not make code changes yet.

prompt_templates.title: Fix one failing check
prompt_templates.prompt: Use iterate-pr to inspect the failed check logs, identify the smallest valid fix, and show me the diff before committing.

prompt_templates.title: Handle review feedback
prompt_templates.prompt: Use iterate-pr to collect review comments and bot feedback. Verify each item, fix valid issues, and ask me about unclear requests.

prompt_templates.title: Iterate until merge ready
prompt_templates.prompt: Use iterate-pr to repeat the feedback, fix, push, and wait cycle until required checks pass. Ask before each push.

output_examples.input: Find why my pull request is failing.
output_examples.output: The skill reports the current PR, lists failing checks, summarizes the failing job logs, and names the files likely needing changes.
The skill separates valid comments from already resolved items, proposes targeted edits, and requests clarification for ambiguous feedback.

output_examples.input: Keep iterating until CI is green.
output_examples.output: The skill applies focused fixes, waits for checks, and stops when checks pass or when repeated failures need user help.

best_practices: Review the diff before any commit or push.
Keep fixes small and tied to one CI failure or comment.
Ask for user guidance when feedback conflicts or repeats.
anti_patterns: Do not push broad changes without reviewing the staged diff.
Do not assume a check name explains the failure.
Do not ignore pending bot checks that may add feedback.

faq.question: Does this skill require GitHub CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. It expects an authenticated GitHub CLI in the repository.

faq.question: Can it make commits and push changes?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow includes committing and pushing, so users should approve those steps.

faq.question: Does it inspect CI logs?
faq.answer: Yes. It tells the agent to read failed workflow logs before changing code.

faq.question: Will it fix every failing check automatically?
faq.answer: No. It should stop and ask for help when failures repeat or need a decision.

faq.question: Can it handle review comments?
faq.answer: Yes. It gathers review, conversation, and bot comments before deciding what to fix.

faq.question: Is it safe for protected branches?
faq.answer: Use it with care. Confirm branch permissions and review changes before any push.
